summary: Implemented the ADR-025 clause 2 read-only diagnostics panel on the existing embedded settings page (Phase 17 task 17.3, goal F3). src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html gains one read-only verticalSection ('Diagnostics') after the Logging section and before the Save button, with a static-hidden empty #diagnosticsPanel container, plus an inline-JS block declaring the fixed 28-leaf diagnosticsCounters table derived from the endpoint contract (QueueDepth/QueueInFlight; SonarrHealth/RadarrHealth; MatchingFailures.NotFound/Ambiguous/Unsupported; CacheHits/CacheMisses; one RenderFailures.<reason> row per declared RenderFailureReason; StaleMetadataTransitions), each with a fixed page label and a stable path-derived element id. On pageshow (after the configuration load request, one call per page show) the panel makes exactly one ApiClient.ajax({ type: 'GET', url: ApiClient.getUrl('ArrTags/Status'), dataType: 'json' }) request; the pinned bundled web client (node_modules.jellyfin-apiclient.bundle.js in the extracted pinned host) was inspected directly: getUrl prepends the server address and a separator, and ajax delegates to fetch which rejects on status >= 400 and parses dataType 'json', so 401/403/404/500 and a malformed body all take the rejection path. The panel is fail-closed: the container starts display:none and empty in the served page, the load path clears it before requesting, the success path renders only a JSON object (a null, array, string, or number body returns without rendering), a render exception is caught and cleared, and the rejection branch clears the panel; the clear path writes only textContent = '' and display: none, so no data and no error/status/endpoint surface is rendered. Rendering is bounded: counts pass typeof value === 'number' && isFinite(value) ? value : 0, health renders only when the value equals one of the declared ArrConnectionHealth names (Unknown/Healthy/Unavailable/AuthenticationFailed/Incompatible) and otherwise Unknown, the fixed table is the only render domain, the response object is never indexed directly by the render, iterated (no Object.keys/for...in), or stringified, and the only textContent assignments are the panel clear, the group heading, the fixed label, and the bounded value. The panel adds no input/select/textarea/button/form element, no configuration property, no write verb, no retry/polling, and no save-path change; the submit handler does not reference the panel and keeps its single configuration read and write. tests/ArrTags.Tests/DiagnosticsStatusPanelTests.cs adds 6 structural cases (the repository has no JavaScript runtime) deriving the expected counter set and health whitelist from the C# model types and the route from ArrTagsStatusController.RoutePrefix, and pinning the fetch helper pair, the bounded fallbacks, the fail-closed branches, the absence of any input/save wiring, and the placement. Nine temporary page probes each failed exactly the intended test and the page was restored byte-identically. ./build.sh build reports 0 warnings / 0 errors (an initial build's 6 xUnit2013 analyzer warnings on literal MatchCollection count assertions in the new test file were rewritten before the final run); the default suite is Failed 0, Passed 1794, Skipped 64, Total 1858 (pre-task baseline after 17.2: Failed 0, Passed 1788, Skipped 64, Total 1852; +6 passed, +6 total, 0 new failures/skips). ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset, so no host-guarded run was performed and the 64 host-guarded skips are unchanged. The panel's inline JavaScript cannot be executed in this environment and the pinned live matrix runs --nowebclient, so the panel is verified structurally against the endpoint model and the pinned web client source, not by a live browser run; the F3 canonical documentation (F3 register entry, architecture 11/12, ADR-025 implementation note, README) and the endpoint/panel security review are the plan-assigned task 17.4, and F3 remains open and the phase gate/tag unapplied.

interpretations.question: Where on the settings page does the panel live, and is the whole section or only the panel container hidden before data arrives?
interpretations.chosen: The section is a new verticalSection placed after the Logging section and before the Save button (one of the locations the task suggests); it stays in the page layout, while the #diagnosticsPanel container is static-hidden (display:none) and empty until a bounded snapshot renders.
interpretations.basis: The task's design constraint names 'after the Logging section / before the Save button' as an acceptable placement; ADR-025 clause 2 and the task allow keeping the panel hidden/empty when the endpoint is not authorized or unavailable. The static heading/description are fixed page copy, not data or an error surface, so they do not violate fail-closed.
interpretations.impact: User-visible fail-closed behavior only; no persisted state, configuration, endpoint, or save-path semantics change. A non-administrator or a failed fetch sees an empty hidden panel with no status detail.

interpretations.question: How is a partial or missing field rendered without exposing a free-form response string?
interpretations.chosen: A count renders only after typeof value === 'number' && isFinite(value) and otherwise renders 0; a health value renders only when it equals one of the declared ArrConnectionHealth names and otherwise renders 'Unknown'. The render iterates only the fixed page table; it never iterates response keys.
interpretations.basis: The task explicitly requires tolerating a missing field with a safe fallback (0/Unknown) rather than failing, and ADR-025 clause 3 fixes the counter set and the bounded enum; the fixed table (not the response) is the render domain.
interpretations.impact: Rendering only. A malformed non-object body still renders nothing (the fail-closed branch); a well-formed object with missing/non-numeric fields renders the documented fallbacks.

interpretations.question: How are the render-failure classifications shown, given the endpoint returns an object with one count per RenderFailureReason?
interpretations.chosen: A fixed 18-row 'Render failures' list, one row per declared RenderFailureReason, including zero counts, with a fixed page label per classification.
interpretations.basis: The task requires rendering the render failures as a bounded list of classification/count pairs rather than raw JSON, and ADR-025 clause 3 fixes the counter set; the classification list is derived from RenderFailureCounts and pinned by the test.
interpretations.impact: Rendering only; adding or removing a classification requires the endpoint and the page table to move together (the new test fails otherwise).

interpretations.question: When is the panel data fetched, and is there a manual refresh?
interpretations.chosen: One GET per pageshow (after the configuration load request); no refresh control and no polling/retry.
interpretations.basis: The task requires a read-only panel with no input and no unbounded retry; the established page pattern loads data on pageshow. A refresh button would add a control, which the task's 'no input, no form field' constraint and the read-only intent disfavor.
interpretations.impact: An administrator sees current process counters each time the settings page is shown; stale values cannot be refreshed without re-showing the page.

known_limitations: The panel's inline JavaScript is not executed by the suite or any live run here. Precondition - the repository deliberately has no JavaScript runtime, this environment has none, and the pinned live matrix runs --nowebclient. Behaviour - the fetch, the DOM construction, the pinned web client's rejection path, and the fail-closed no-data rendering are verified structurally (the counter set and health whitelist derived from the C# model, the route from ArrTagsStatusController.RoutePrefix, the helper pair verified against the pinned bundled web client source in /tmp/arrtags-host-dl/host/jellyfin/jellyfin-web/node_modules.jellyfin-apiclient.bundle.js), not executed in a browser. Consequence - a browser/runtime behavior change in ApiClient.ajax or in the page script would not be caught by the suite; the F3 security review (task 17.4) is the plan-assigned place to adjudicate this residual, which matches the existing V12-G8-1-style accepted page limitation.

No host-guarded run was performed: ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset in this environment, so the default suite reports the same 64 host-guarded skips as the pre-task baseline, and the host's route discovery of the controller and its live 401/403/200 behavior are not exercised here (they were pinned in 17.2 by the host-guarded policy-name fact and the in-process MVC harness).

The F3 canonical documentation is deliberately deferred to the plan-assigned task 17.4 and F3 remains Open: docs/limitations/open.md F3 and docs/architecture/12-performance-and-operational-limits.md still describe the status surface as not implemented, and the README, architecture 11, and ADR-025 do not yet record the shipped endpoint/panel. This task was explicitly scoped to the changelog/PLANS/state surfaces and the F3 documentation and security review is task 17.4 (v1.2 plan section 7, phase 17 checklist), so those files were not edited; a reviewer should read them as pending 17.4, not as verified-current.

The panel reports process-lifetime counters that reset when Jellyfin restarts (ADR-025 consequence), and only the fixed bounded values are rendered; there is no per-item listing, history, or export. This is the accepted ADR-025 shape, not a defect of this task.
